tests.title: Default-off server starts and serves /api/vehicles with no telemetry output
tests.rationale: "Is it alive" with the preload wired in must be proved through the real entry path. A unit test cannot show that adding the preload leaves the default server unchanged.

tests.title: Enabled server exports a span for /api/vehicles to a loopback collector
tests.rationale: The critical path (preload, instrumentation patching, OTLP export) only works end to end in a real process. This is the single feature-is-alive check.
traces_to: risk: ESM and `tsx` can stop auto-instrumentation from patching modules if the SDK loads too late

tests.title: Disabled telemetry makes no connection to a collector
tests.gherkin:
Given a fake collector is listening on 127.0.0.1
And the server is started with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT pointing at it and OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles several times
Then every response is 200
And the collector has accepted zero connections
And the server's stdout and stderr contain no "telemetry" text
tests.rationale: "Makes no network calls" can only be observed from outside the process, with a listening socket to count connections. The unit layer proves the decision, not the absence of traffic.

tests.title: Request produces a span with method, route, status and service name
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running with telemetry enabled against the fake collector
And OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=warehouse-server-test
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles
Then the collector receives POST /v1/traces
And the payload contains a server span with http method GET, a route containing /api/vehicles and status code 200
And the resource service.name is "warehouse-server-test"
tests.rationale: Proves the OTLP payload as a collector sees it, which the in-memory component test cannot (serialisation, resource, real HTTP).
traces_to: risk: The OpenTelemetry JS packages move quickly and have separate experimental and stable version lines, so versions may be mismatched

tests.title: HTTP server metrics are exported
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running with telemetry enabled and a short OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles
Then the collector receives POST /v1/metrics
And the payload contains an HTTP server request duration metric with at least one data point
tests.rationale: HTTP server metrics come from instrumentation-http on real node:http. app.inject may not drive them, so the real path is the reliable proof.

tests.title: A 5xx response is an error span and a 4xx is not
tests.gherkin:
Given the fixture server (src/test-support/server-fixture.ts) is running with FIXTURE_FAIL_LIST=1 and the preload flag
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles and receives 500
And the client calls GET /api/vehicles/999999 and receives 404
Then the collector receives a span for the 500 request with error status
And the span for the 404 request does not have error status
tests.rationale: Confirms the error status survives export over real HTTP. The status-mapping logic itself is proved lower (T-17, T-18).

tests.title: Exporter headers are applied but never logged
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="authorization=Bearer secret-test-token"
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles and the exporter flushes
Then the collector receives the authorization header on its export request
And the server's stdout and stderr do not contain "secret-test-token"
tests.rationale: Needs the real exporter to show the header is sent, and real process output to show it is not logged.
traces_to: risk: Telemetry leaks sensitive data (headers, credentials, VINs, query strings)

tests.title: Request bodies, VINs and query strings are not exported
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running with telemetry enabled
When the client POSTs a vehicle with a known VIN in the body
And the client calls GET /api/vehicles?make=Ford
Then the exported trace payload does not contain the VIN or any part of the request body
And no exported attribute holds the query string value
tests.rationale: Repeats the in-process leakage check (T-19) over real HTTP, where instrumentation-http records url.query/http.target differently from inject.
traces_to: risk: Telemetry leaks sensitive data (headers, credentials, VINs, query strings)

tests.title: Non-local plain-HTTP endpoint is refused and the server still runs
tests.gherkin:
Given OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://collector.example.com
When the server is started
Then it serves GET /api/vehicles with 200
And it prints exactly one "telemetry disabled" warning
And the warning does not contain the endpoint URL
And no outbound connection to that host is attempted
tests.rationale: "No connection attempted" and "server keeps running" are process-level facts. The rule itself is unit-tested (T-27).

tests.title: Unreachable collector does not affect responses or crash the server
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running with the collector endpoint pointing at a closed loopback port
When the client sends several requests
Then every response is 200 within a loose latency bound
And the server process is still running afterwards
tests.rationale: Failed exports happen on background timers in the real batch processors. Only a real process shows they do not surface in request handling.
traces_to: risk: The exporter adds overhead or fails when the collector is down

tests.title: SIGTERM flushes pending telemetry and exits 0
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running against the fake collector with a long OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
And one request has been served
When the process receives SIGTERM
Then it exits with code 0 within 10 seconds
And the collector has received the span for that request
tests.rationale: Signal handling in index.ts and the real batch flush cannot be proved in-process.

tests.title: Shutdown stays bounded when the collector never replies
tests.gherkin:
Given a collector that accepts connections but never responds
And the server is running against it and has served a request
When the process receives SIGTERM
Then the process exits within the shutdown bound
tests.rationale: Proves the real process cannot hang on a stuck collector. The timeout logic is unit-tested separately (T-21).
traces_to: risk: The exporter adds overhead or fails when the collector is down

tests.title: Preload makes both HTTP and Fastify instrumentation take effect
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is started with the start-script command shape (--import ./src/instrument.ts)
And telemetry is enabled against the fake collector
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles
Then the exported spans include one from the HTTP instrumentation scope
And the exported spans include one from the Fastify instrumentation scope with the route name
tests.rationale: AC-9 is about load order in the real entry path. Both scopes present shows both node:http and Fastify were patched, so a late-loaded SDK would fail here.
traces_to: risk: ESM and `tsx` can stop auto-instrumentation from patching modules if the SDK loads too late

tests.title: Standard sampler variable is honoured
tests.gherkin:
Given the server is running with telemetry enabled and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_off
When the client calls GET /api/vehicles
Then the collector receives no trace spans for the request
tests.rationale: Shows sampling is controlled only by OTEL_* variables in the real SDK. There is no repo code to unit test, since the SDK does the selection.

tests.title: Default-off initTelemetry({}) returns undefined and emits nothing
tests.rationale: The initTelemetry and buildApp boundary is what existing tests rely on. Proves they need no collector, so existing suites are unaffected. Spies on console.warn and checks the memory exporter is empty after app.inject.

tests.title: GET /api/vehicles span carries method, route, status and default service name
tests.rationale: Span content can be asserted exactly with an in-memory exporter, without a process or network. Checks http.route (or installed equivalent) contains /api/vehicles, method, status 200, and resource service.name is warehouse-server.
traces_to: risk: The OpenTelemetry JS packages move quickly and have separate experimental and stable version lines, so versions may be mismatched

tests.title: Handled 4xx responses are not error spans
tests.rationale: This is the LLP open question (does @fastify/otel mark handled 4xx as ERROR?). It must be decided before the contingent app.ts change, and the in-memory exporter answers it fastest. Asserts no span has status code ERROR.

tests.title: A 5xx response produces a span with error status
tests.rationale: The existing error handler logs and returns 500, so the logic is provable in-process. The response body must also still be the existing generic 500 body.

tests.title: No VIN, body or query string appears in span attributes
tests.rationale: A cheap assertion over every attribute key and value of every finished span. It runs far faster than the e2e version (T-8) and fails first if an option such as requestHook is added.
traces_to: risk: Telemetry leaks sensitive data (headers, credentials, VINs, query strings)

tests.title: Metrics are recorded and flushed on shutdown
tests.rationale: Shows the metric reader is wired and that shutdownTelemetry() flushes data points. If inject does not drive HTTP server metrics, this test is dropped in favour of T-5 and T-11, as the LLP notes.

tests.title: shutdownTelemetry is bounded when an exporter never finishes
tests.target: tools/warehouse-server/src/telemetry.test.ts (span processor override whose shutdown() never resolves; shutdownTelemetry(100))
tests.rationale: Exercises the Promise.race timeout and the unref'd timer deterministically, which an e2e run can only show with timing slack. Asserts it resolves in roughly the timeout and does not reject.
traces_to: risk: The exporter adds overhead or fails when the collector is down

tests.title: Invalid endpoint leaves telemetry off with one safe warning
tests.target: tools/warehouse-server/src/telemetry.test.ts (initTelemetry with http://collector.example.com and an authorization header value)
tests.rationale: Crosses the resolveTelemetryConfig and initTelemetry boundary. Asserts it returns undefined, does not throw, calls console.warn once, the message has neither the URL nor the header value, and no span is recorded.

tests.title: initTelemetry is idempotent and shutdownTelemetry acts on the same instance
tests.rationale: The preload and index.ts share one module-level SDK. If a second call created a second SDK, index.ts would flush the wrong one. Asserts a second initTelemetry returns the existing handle and one shutdownTelemetry flushes spans.

tests.title: No endpoint, or only empty endpoint values, gives disabled with no reason
tests.rationale: Pure branching logic. This is the default-off decision, and the missing reason is what makes initTelemetry silent.

tests.title: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED overrides a valid endpoint, case-insensitive
tests.rationale: A single pure branch. Covers true, TRUE and True; false leaves telemetry enabled.

tests.title: Loopback HTTP and any HTTPS endpoint are accepted
tests.rationale: Boundary table of the HTTPS rule, no I/O needed.

tests.title: Non-local plain HTTP is rejected with a reason that omits the URL
tests.target: tools/warehouse-server/src/telemetry.test.ts (http://collector.example.com gives enabled false with a reason)
tests.rationale: Pure function with a security-relevant output: fail closed and no leakage of the host or URL in the reason.

tests.title: Unparsable, lookalike-host and userinfo endpoints are rejected safely
tests.rationale: Edge cases for the hostname allow-list (exact match, not prefix) and credentials in the URL. Asserts the reason never contains the credentials or URL and that the function does not throw.

tests.title: Traces-only and metrics-only endpoint variables get the same check
tests.target: tools/warehouse-server/src/telemetry.test.ts (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT; valid general plus invalid per-signal gives disabled)
tests.rationale: Validates every set endpoint, so one bad value cannot slip through behind a good one.

tests.title: service.name defaults to warehouse-server and honours OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
tests.rationale: Pure default and override logic.

tests.title: Header values never appear in a config result
tests.target: tools/warehouse-server/src/telemetry.test.ts (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS set with valid and invalid endpoints; JSON.stringify of the result must not contain the value)
tests.rationale: Cheap guard against a regression that echoes the environment into a reason or config object.
traces_to: risk: Telemetry leaks sensitive data (headers, credentials, VINs, query strings)

tests.title: shutdownTelemetry is a no-op when nothing was started
tests.rationale: Pure guard branch. It matters because index.ts calls it on every shutdown, including the default-off path. Asserts it resolves, does not throw and leaves no timer open.

tests.title: dev and start scripts preload instrument.ts; other scripts are unchanged
tests.rationale: npm run dev uses tsx watch, which is slow and flaky to spawn in a test. A static check on the script strings is the lowest layer that proves dev is wired, while T-2 and T-13 prove the same flag works for start. Accepts the documented fallback form (node --import tsx --import ./src/instrument.ts). Asserts the instrument.ts import comes before src/index.ts and that typecheck and test are unchanged.

tests.title: Import graph keeps the load-order guarantee
tests.rationale: Static check. instrument.ts imports only ./telemetry.js (plus optional node:module), index.ts does not import instrument.ts, and telemetry.ts does not import fastify or node:http. Any of these breaking would silently disable instrumentation.
traces_to: risk: ESM and `tsx` can stop auto-instrumentation from patching modules if the SDK loads too late

tests.title: No hardcoded endpoint, token or credential in new source
tests.target: tools/warehouse-server/src/telemetry.repo.test.ts (scan telemetry.ts, instrument.ts, test-support/server-fixture.ts; check .gitignore still ignores .env)
tests.rationale: Static scan. Asserts no http(s):// literal other than the loopback allow-list names, no Bearer string, and no console call that references exporter header values.

tests.title: Dependencies are declared only in the server package and resolved in the lock file
tests.rationale: Offline check. Asserts the four runtime packages are in the server's dependencies with caret ranges, nothing is added to the root package.json, each resolves in package-lock.json, and @opentelemetry/api resolves to a single version (no duplicate majors).
traces_to: risk: New dependencies enlarge the workspace install and the lock file
risk: The OpenTelemetry JS packages move quickly and have separate experimental and stable version lines, so versions may be mismatched

tests.title: README documents the variables, the HTTPS rule and a local collector example
tests.rationale: Documentation content is a static check. Asserts every OTEL_* variable from the LLP list appears, the HTTPS-for-non-local rule and the default-off statement are present, a loopback example (127.0.0.1:4318) exists, and any container image named uses registry.redhat.io.

gaps: AC-13 'latest stable', 'actively maintained' and 'no known high or critical vulnerabilities' are not automated: they depend on the live registry and advisory database, so a test would be non-deterministic and need network. They are checked at implementation time with npm outdated and npm audit. T-36 covers only the offline parts (declared, pinned by lock file, scoped to the server).

AC-11 'no new warnings' and 'existing suites pass unchanged' are not a new test: they are proved by running the existing npm run test:warehouse, npm run typecheck and npm test -w @warehouse/server. New tests (T-15, T-16, T-33) cover only the new-test part of the criterion.

The npm run dev command (tsx watch) is not spawned: its preload is checked statically (T-33) and the same flag is exercised through the start shape (T-2, T-13). Spawning a file watcher in CI is flaky and adds nothing beyond that.

The SDK start-failure branch in initTelemetry (sdk.start() throwing, warn and return undefined) has no dedicated test: it cannot be induced without mocking the SDK, which the repo does not do elsewhere. T-10 and T-22 cover the user-visible fail-closed behaviour for realistic failures.
Risk: the issue is under-specified and the scope may differ. This is a product decision, not testable, and remains an open question in the plans.
Risk: node:sqlite has no auto-instrumentation so database time is invisible. Accepted in the HLP with no database spans in this issue, so there is nothing to test.
OTLP over gRPC is not tested: the plans document HTTP (JSON or protobuf) only.
Frontends (sales-orders-ui, tools/warehouse-ui) and the Java model are out of scope and not tested.
The contingent app.ts change for 4xx spans has no separate test: T-17 triggers it and then verifies it, and T-18 also guards that the 500 response body is unchanged.
